summary: 4/5 statins fail engine Cmax validation due to stiff MM kinetics at saturated abundance. Pravastatin is the only statin that solves. Neither LSODA (scipy) nor Kvaerno5 (JAX/diffrax) converges in reasonable time for the other four.

per_drug_results.status: STIFF — ON mode fails on both backends
STIFF — highest Jmax/lowest Cmax, most aggressive

root_cause_hypothesis: At abundance = 1.0e11 (pravastatin-calibrated), the effective uptake rate k_eff = (Jmax / Km) × abundance = 1e11 × (170/6.5) ≈ 2.6e12 pmol/s per uM for rosuvastatin. This is several orders of magnitude faster than hepatic blood flow (87 L/h ≈ 3.6e-5 * avogadro-like factor), creating a stiff ratio > 1e6. Pravastatin's higher Km (13.6) pushes it into the capacity-limited regime where the numerator is essentially Jmax (constant) rather than nonlinear, avoiding the stiffness.

remediation_path.short_term: None — switching solvers does not resolve; both LSODA and Kvaerno5 stall.
long_term: Option A: recalibrate liver.OATP1B1 abundance downward (try 1e9 or 1e10) so 4/5 statins operate in the non-saturated regime. This matches Phase 2B finding that clinical SLCO1B1 AUC effects require non-saturated regime.
Option B: introduce a per-drug effective abundance scaling based on known hepatic uptake CL, so each statin lands in its own non-saturated regime.
Option C: implement flow-limited extraction approximation for saturated-regime drugs — bypass MM kinetics at high Jmax/abundance with analytical well-stirred extraction.
remediation_path.recommendation: Option A. Phase 2B already surfaces that abundance 1e11 is flow-limited. A coordinated re-calibration unlocks both Phase 2A (directional fold error reduction) and Phase 2B (SLCO1B1 phenotype directional Cmax response).

conclusion: Phase 2A engine validation is BLOCKED on abundance re-calibration, not on solver choice. Solver switch (scipy → JAX Kvaerno5) does not close the gap. Per-drug probe (this diagnosis) replaces the prior 'LSODA stall' hypothesis — the stall is physical (stiff ODE), not numerical-transient.
